html:
RealPLKSR (neosr, after PLKSR by Lee et al., 2024): a large-kernel CNN upscaler; realplksr-nomoswebphoto-x4 is Philip Hofmann's x4 model for noisy, blurred and JPEG / WebP-compressed photos; also loads other RealPLKSR checkpoints. Apache-2.0 code, CC-BY-4.0 weights.

Commercial use: yes.

Details
  • Original code: https://github.com/neosr-project/neosr at 31c7022620c6
  • Code licence: Apache-2.0 (permissive); files: LICENSE
  • Weights licence: CC-BY-4.0
  • Licence evidence: https://github.com/neosr-project/neosr/blob/31c7022620c682cf0961c8634d60787179145c5b/license.txt ; https://github.com/Phhofm/models/releases/tag/4xNomosWebPhoto_RealPLKSR
  • Training data: Nomos-v2 (neosr's 6000-image multipurpose super-resolution set) (Release notes: Nomos-v2 (6000 photos, neosr's dataset) with realistic noise, lens blur, JPEG and WebP degradations; pretrained from neosr's 4x_realplksr_gan_pretrain.)
  • Kernel libraries: cudnn_hacc
  • Variants: realplksr-nomoswebphoto-x4
  • Outputs: image
  • Input size: any H x W >= 1, resized or padded inside the model
  • Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): realplksr-nomoswebphoto-x4 512x512 (0.2 GiB peak allocated, 0.3 reserved)
  • realplksr-nomoswebphoto-x4 512x512, first call: portable + torch.compile 15 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 26 s (ONNX + engine).
  • realplksr-nomoswebphoto-x4 original 512x512: .half() on 1 modules, fp16 inputs; neosr realplksr eval mode, float32, net(lq) clamped
  • realplksr-nomoswebphoto-x4 load / first call: original 0.21 s / 0.759 s, portable 0.18 s / 0.414 s, kernels 0.56 s / 0.253 s
  • Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

Measured

DIV2K validation HR images and the official bicubic LR images (x4 or x2, the model's scale), one pass without tiles; PSNR and SSIM (Gaussian 11 x 11, sigma 1.5) on the Y channel (BT.601) of the output rounded to uint8, scale px border cropped, averaged over the images. Real-ESRGAN is trained for real-world degradations, not bicubic, so its PSNR is low: the numbers compare our modes with the original, not with PSNR-oriented upscalers. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.
